//: Explicit allowlist of image sources. A candidate from a domain absent from this file is rejected before a byte is downloaded. Extending it is a deliberate edit to this file, reviewed like any other change - the pipeline never widens it at runtime.
//trust: 0-100. Feeds the sourceTrust term of the quality score. Only 'manufacturer' sources are official product renders; 'encyclopedic' is a volunteer photograph of a device and is accepted only when it survives every composition rule.

upload.wikimedia.org.note: Wikimedia Commons file store. Explicit licence per file, which is why it is usable at all; photography is volunteer-contributed and frequently a shop shelf or a desk, so composition rules do the work here.

commons.wikimedia.org.note: Commons API host. Metadata only; files themselves come from upload.wikimedia.org.

thumb.wikimedia.org.note: Wikimedia's rendition host. Added deliberately after requesting sized renditions made Commons serve from here instead of upload.wikimedia.org, and every candidate was correctly refused as off-allowlist. Same operator and same files as upload.wikimedia.org - it serves the /thumb/ derivatives of them - so it carries the same trust and no more.

//manufacturer: Official product-render sources go here when one is available. None is configured, and that is a statement rather than an omission: images.samsung.com, www.apple.com and i01.appmifile.com all serve official renders behind per-product paths that are not derivable from a TAC record, so reaching them needs either a licensed catalogue feed or a per-vendor adapter with the vendor's agreement. The pipeline is built to take one - add the domain here with type 'manufacturer' and implement a provider - and until then it will not pretend an encyclopedia photograph is a product render.
